Article Title: GST collections cross Rs 2 lakh crore again, rise 14.7% in September
Article Text:
Revenue from domestic transactions grew 10.1% to Rs 1.38 lakh crore in September 2026, compared with Rs 1.25 lakh crore in the corresponding month last year.

India’s gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections once again crossed the Rs 2 lakh crore mark in September, rising 14.7% year-on-year to Rs 2.04 lakh crore, according to government data. The increase was driven by higher revenue from both domestic transactions and imports.Revenue from domestic transactions grew 10.1% to Rs 1.38 lakh crore in September 2026, compared with Rs 1.25 lakh crore in the corresponding month last year. GST revenue from imports, meanwhile, rose 25.9% year-on-year to Rs 65,525 crore from Rs 52,031 crore.Gross Integrated GST (IGST) collections increased to Rs 1.20 lakh crore during the month, against Rs 1.02 lakh crore in September 2025. Central GST collections stood at Rs 37,762 crore, while State GST collections were at Rs 45,363 crore.The rise in gross collections came even as GST refunds declined during the month. Total refunds stood at Rs 27,001 crore in September, down 3% from Rs 27,848 crore a year earlier.According to Abhishek Jain, indirect tax head & partner at KPMG, the growth in GST collections is encouraging, but the sharp rise in import GST needs to be examined further.“Gross GST collections growing 14.7% in September despite global headwinds is very encouraging. As import GST is up nearly 26%; it's important to see how much of that is raw materials versus finished goods.”Jain further added, “It’ll be good to analyse this in detail, specifically if it signals already stronger domestic manufacturing or there is a need for further push, thereby making stronger the case for continuing and expanding schemes like PLI.”Domestic refunds fell 13.5% year-on-year to Rs 13,504 crore. In contrast, export GST refunds processed through ICEGATE rose 10.2% to Rs 13,497 crore.With refunds taken into account, net GST collections grew faster than gross collections. Net revenue rose 18.1% year-on-year to Rs 1.77 lakh crore in September, compared with Rs 1.50 lakh crore in September 2025.Net domestic GST revenue increased 13.5% to Rs 1.24 lakh crore, while net revenue from customs-related GST jumped 30.8% to Rs 52,028 crore.The September figures also pushed up the GST collection tally for the first six months of the financial year. Between April and September, gross GST collections rose 11.6% to Rs 12.46 lakh crore, compared with Rs 11.17 lakh crore in the same period of 2025-26.Net GST collections during the April-September period increased 10.4% to Rs 10.66 lakh crore from Rs 9.65 lakh crore a year earlier.In terms of states, Maharashtra emerged as the largest contributor among the states listed, recording GST revenue of Rs 29,986 crore in September, a 15% year-on-year increase. Karnataka's collections rose 16% to Rs 13,884 crore, while Gujarat recorded Rs 12,222 crore, up 17%.Uttar Pradesh and Telangana both registered 18% growth in GST revenue during the month. Uttar Pradesh collected Rs 8,882 crore, while Telangana recorded Rs 5,327 crore.Commenting on the numbers, Manoj Mishra, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat said, “September GST collections are encouraging, but the headline Rs 2.04 lakh crore is only one part of the story. Gross collections grew 14.7% year-on-year, with domestic GST revenue rising 10.1%, while import-linked GST grew a much sharper 25.9%.”“The continued strength in the import component is noteworthy, particularly against the backdrop of elevated energy prices, geopolitical disruptions and higher landed costs for globally traded commodities. It therefore provides an important boost to collections but should not be interpreted entirely as a proxy for stronger domestic consumption,” he says.“Against this backdrop, the forthcoming 57th GST Council meeting holds significance. If the Council can translate GST 2.0 into meaningful process reforms around ITC, registration, refunds and compliance, it could strengthen the quality of revenue growth by reducing friction for compliant businesses and improving tax efficiency. The next phase of GST, therefore, is less about headline rate changes and more about making the system work better and that could provide an important foundation for sustaining the current momentum,” he adds.
Article Summary: Revenue from domestic transactions grew 10.1% to Rs 1.38 lakh crore in September 2026. GST revenue from imports, meanwhile, rose 25.9% year-on-year to Rs 65,525 crore. Central GST collections stood at Rs 37,762 crore, while State GST collections were at Rs 45,363 crore.

Article Title: Why stock market was down today? Rs 6 lakh crore wiped out; Sensex, Nifty suffer worst losing streak in 25 years
Article Text:
Bloodbath at Dalal Street

FII selling intensifies

US bond yields hit multi-year highs

Rupee remains under pressure

Crude close to $100

Auto and infra stocks drag D-Street

Nifty’s key psychological levels breached

NEW DELHI: Dalal Street suffered its worst and longest losing streak in nearly 25 years, with investors losing over Rs 6 lakh crore. Benchmark indices came under heavy selling pressure on Thursday, with BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 falling more than 1% as persistent foreign investor outflows, rising US bond yields and pressure on rupee weighed down sentiments.During the session, the BSE Sensex plunged more than 1,000 points to fall below the 71,600 mark, while the NSE Nifty50 dropped over 300 points to slip below 22,300. The indices, however, pared some of their losses later in the session. Sensex eventually closed 570.59 points, or 0.79%, lower at 71,909.70, while Nifty50 fell 205.40 points, or 0.91%, to settle at 22,282.75.This brutal selloff the dragged total market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE to Rs 466 lakh crore.With this fall, D-Street has marked the fifth consecutive day of ending in red due to a mix of factors like crude prices, economic indicators and geopolitical cues. According to Vinit Bolinjkar, head of research, September remained a weak month overall. "The Nifty fell for seven straight weeks, pressured by volatile crude oil prices, rising global bond yields, and steady FII selling. Within this, auto, realty, consumer durables and financial services held up better and even posted gains on value buying, while IT and Pharma dragged the index down due to weak global demand cues and currency-related concerns.Broader markets (mid and small caps) were more volatile than large caps during the month."As markets will remain closed on Friday, investors turned cautious ahead of the extended break. Here are the key factors behind Thursday’s selloff on Dalal Street:Foreign investors remained a major source of pressure on Indian equities, turning net sellers across all reported equity and debt segments in September for the first time in two years. They sold Indian equities worth $1.06 billion on Wednesday, while exchange data showed FII selling of Rs 10,148.41 crore on the same day.Their selling over the previous five sessions stood at about $3.6 billion, taking their year-to-date selling to a record $27.8 billion."The sustained FII selling became intense during the last two trading days when the FIIs sold equity for a total of Rs 20,128 crore. With the US 10-year bond yield rising further to 5.3 per cent, FIIs may continue to sell. An apparent contradiction in the FII activity is that even while selling through the exchanges, they have been consistently investing through the primary market and also buying expensive mid and smallcaps," V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist, Geojit Investments Limited, said.FPIs had been net buyers in equities in July and August, with purchases of Rs 20,200 crore and Rs 29,631 crore, respectively. However, they were net sellers of Rs 35,861 crore in stocks till September 29. After another Rs 10,148 crore of selling on September 30, the month's total stock selling stood at about Rs 46,000 crore, according to NSDL and BSE data.For the current year, FPI net selling in equities has reached Rs 2.6 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.7 lakh crore in the previous year. The 2026 outflow is now the highest-ever annual net selling figure, NSDL data showed.Rising US treasury yields added to the pressure on equities. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.31%, its highest level since 2007. It rose more than 87 basis points during the September quarter, marking its biggest quarterly increase since 1994, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters.The 30-year Treasury yield also moved above 5.65%, reaching its highest level since 2002.Higher bond yields can make debt markets more attractive to investors, putting pressure on riskier equity markets. Bond yields move inversely to bond prices, so the sharp rise in yields reflected an intense selloff in bonds."The domestic market remains under pressure after extending its decline, with September marking the Nifty's steepest monthly fall since March. Foreign selling and elevated global borrowing costs continue to weigh on sentiment, although the easing in crude prices and softer US inflation provide some counterweight," Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder & CEO of HST Wealth, a research analyst firm, said.Rupee fell 0.16% to 95.9850 per dollar as the dollar index rose to a more than three-month high amid higher US Treasury yields. Losses were limited as state-run banks sold dollars, likely on behalf of the RBI, Reuters reported.Anil Bhansali, head of advisory at Finrex Treasury Advisors, said that the 96 against the greenback is a crucial level."The 96 level remains an important psychological and technical area, with the rupee showing some resilience each time it approaches that level, thanks largely due to the Reserve Bank of India."In afternoon trade, Brent crude inched 1.87% high to trade around $99.86 per barrel, while WTI crude gained 2.01% to $92.24 per barrel. Brent crude futures have continued to remain near $97 a barrel after Tehran said it had received Washington's response to its latest ceasefire proposal.Crude oil prices remain a critical bellwether for the equity markets. Because India imports over 85% of its crude oil requirements, fluctuations in global energy prices directly ripple through the country's macroeconomic fundamentals.The selloff was broad-based, with several heavyweight stocks coming under pressure. Among the 30 Sensex companies, Mahindra & Mahindra, Maruti, UltraTech Cement, Bharat Electronics, Eternal and Asian Paints were among the major laggards.Maruti fell 4.93%, M&M 4.24%, Tata Steel 4.20%, Adani Ports 3.47%, ITC 3.20%, UltraTech Cement 3.01%, Power Grid 2.76% and Eternal 2.75%.Other major losers included HUL, BEL, Trent, NTPC, Larsen & Toubro, Bajaj Finance, Reliance Industries, Titan, IndiGo and Bharti Airtel.In contrast, Infosys, HDFC Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and HCL Tech were among the stocks showing gains during the session. Axis Bank, TCS and ICICI Bank were also among the stocks in the green or near-flat zone.US markets ended mostly lower on Wednesday, adding to the cautious mood in domestic equities.The market decline was also exacerbated after the benchmark indices broke through key technical levels.The Nifty had closed at 22,620 on Wednesday. Hemang Gor, senior research analyst of derivatives and technical research, as cited by ET, identified 22,500 as the index's first support level and warned that a break below it could expose the benchmark to a fall towards 22,400.The Nifty subsequently moved below the second support level as well.Axis Securities had also identified 22,500 as the first support level and said a break below it could drag the index towards 22,300. “Conversely, a sustained move above 22,800 could strengthen the upward momentum, opening the door for a move toward the 23,000–23,100 zone,” said Axis Securities.Meanwhile, "With markets to be closed tomorrow, the session is seeing cautious positioning ahead of the extended break," said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of HST Wealth.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 fall more than 1% as persistent foreign investor outflows, rising US bond yields and pressure on rupee weighed down sentiments. FPI net selling in equities has reached Rs 2.6 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.7 lakh crore in the previous year.

Article Title: Public sector banks to stay closed on Saturdays? PIB debunks fake government notification
Article Text:
PIB debunks fake Saturday holiday notification (representative image)

What PIB Fact Check said

Five-day banking week demand remains under discussion

What the government has actually notified

The Press Information Bureau (PIB) Fact Check unit on Thursday debunked a document circulating on social media that claimed the Central Government had declared every Saturday a public holiday for all public sector banks, including the State Bank of India (SBI).In a post on X, PIB Fact Check said the purported Gazette, which was attributed to the ministry of finance's department of financial services, was fake and that no such notification had been issued by the finance ministry.“A Gazette circulating on social media, purportedly issued by the Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services), claims that the Central Government has declared every Saturday a public holiday for all Public Sector Banks, including SBI,” PIB Fact Check said.It added, “The document being circulated is Fake. No such notification has been issued by @FinMinIndia declaring every Saturday as public holiday for public sector banks.”The fact-check unit also urged people to flag suspicious content related to the Central Government through PIB Fact Check.The fake document comes against the backdrop of the long-standing demand for a five-day banking week.The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) had recently deferred its proposed three-day nationwide strike after reaching an understanding with the Indian Banks' Association (IBA). One of the key issues discussed was the demand to declare the remaining Saturdays as holidays.Under the understanding, a high-level committee comprising representatives of the IBA and UFBU will examine the issue, explore possible alternatives and consult stakeholders, including customers, according to the UFBU circular.The unions had earlier planned the September 28-30 strike with five-day banking among their key demands. The agitation was deferred after the IBA gave assurances on the issue and other matters.The PIB clarification makes clear that there is no notification declaring every Saturday a public holiday for public sector banks.The recent agreement between the IBA and UFBU only provided for discussions through a committee on the demand for declaring the remaining Saturdays as holidays.It did not amount to a government notification implementing a five-day banking week.
Article Summary: PIB Fact Check unit debunked a document circulating on social media. The document claimed the Central Government had declared every Saturday a public holiday for all public sector banks, including the State Bank of India (SBI) The purported Gazette, which was attributed to the ministry of finance's department of financial services, was fake, PIB said.

Article Title: LPG price hike: 19-kg commercial cylinder gets Rs 62.50 costlier; new Aadhaar rule kicks in for domestic users
Article Text:
Commercial LPG gets costlier

The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has risen by Rs 62.50 from Thursday, October 1, taking the price to Rs 2,810. This follows a Rs 9.50 increase in September, when the cylinder was priced at Rs 2,747.50. ATF prices have also gone up by around Rs 16 per litre, from Rs 121 to Rs 137 per litre.The changes come as domestic LPG consumers face a new requirement from October 1, 2026. Those seeking to book refills at the regulated Retail Selling Price (RSP) with applicable subsidy will now need to have completed Biometric Aadhaar Authentication (BAA).The authentication requirement is aimed at ensuring that subsidised LPG reaches genuine and deserving households. Each LPG connection is linked to an Aadhaar-authenticated consumer to prevent diversion of subsidised domestic cylinders for commercial and industrial use, remove duplicate and ineligible connections, and make subsidy delivery more targeted and transparent.Consumers who have already completed BAA will not need to repeat the process and can continue booking refills as before. Those who have not completed it will be able to book a refill at the RSP with subsidy once their authentication is completed.Consumers can complete the authentication process through several channels. During refill delivery, the delivery person can carry out BAA on the spot using the OMC mobile application.The process can also be completed by visiting the LPG distributor's showroom. Consumers can alternatively complete it themselves from home through their OMC's mobile application: IndianOil ONE for Indane customers, HelloBPCL for Bharatgas customers and HP PAY for HP Gas customers.Consumers who are unwilling or unable to complete BAA can still receive LPG. They will have to register their choice through their OMC's digital channels, including the consumer web portal, mobile app, WhatsApp chatbot, IVRS or other available channels.In such cases, LPG will be supplied at the applicable market price without subsidy, in 5-kg or 10-kg cylinders, subject to local availability with the OMC.Consumers who have not yet completed BAA have been urged to do so through any of the available channels, which are accessible in both urban and rural areas.
Article Summary: The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has risen by Rs 62.50 from Thursday, October 1. This follows a Rs 9.50 increase in September, when the cylinder was priced at Rs 2,747.50. ATF prices have also gone up by around Rs 16 per litre, from Rs 121 to Rs 137.

Article Title: Railways fast-tracks Gangtok link as Sivok-Rangpo nears completion
Article Text:
The proposed line will extend the railway network from Rangpo to Gangtok. (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: In a push to bring Sikkim’s capital Gangtok on the railway map, railway ministry has prioritised the plan for a 34-km rail link between Rangpo and Gangtok, estimated to cost around Rs 9,000 crore.TOI has learnt that the proposed link was taken up by Integrated Multimodal Network Planning Group (NPG), the multi-modal evaluation body under PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, last week.The proposed line will extend the railway network from Rangpo to Gangtok once the ongoing link between Sivok in Darjeeling and Rangpo in East Sikkim project is completed. The move comes as the railways targets completion of the long-delayed Sivok-Rangpo railway line by Dec 2027.The 44.5-km Sivok-Rangpo line, being built at an estimated cost of Rs 17,124 crore, will provide the first direct rail connectivity to Sikkim. The project has faced delays due to the challenging Himalayan terrain, requiring construction of several tunnels and major bridges.The railways has been working to extend rail connectivity to the capitals of the north-eastern states. At present, four state capitals in the region have rail connectivity.With Sivok-Rangpo and the proposed Rangpo-Gangtok link, Sikkim would become the next state in the region to get a railway connection to its capital.Officials said the Rangpo-Gangtok extension is being examined now so that work on the next leg can be taken forward without a significant gap after the Sivok-Rangpo section becomes operational. The proposed link is expected to improve access to Gangtok and strengthen connectivity for passengers, tourism and movement of goods.The Sivok-Rangpo project has achieved around 75% physical progress and is targeted for completion by the end of 2027. The section has 14 tunnels and 13 major bridges.While reviewing the progress of the Sivok-Rangpo link in 2021, PM Narendra Modi had asked the ministry to hold officials accountable for the delay.
Article Summary: The proposed line will extend the railway network from Rangpo to Gangtok. The 44.5-km Sivok-Rangpo line, being built at an estimated cost of Rs 17,124 crore, will provide the first direct rail connectivity to Sikkim. The project has faced delays due to the challenging Himalayan terrain.

Article Title: Goyal pitches India as global trade hub, eyes 75-80% of world economy
Article Text:
Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal addresses the US Indian Community Foundation event

$30 trillion economy target

US business, investment and innovation

Government support for businesses

India is building a network of free trade relationships that could eventually cover nearly 75-80 per cent of the world's economies, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said in Chicago, pitching the country as an expanding base for global trade and investment.Addressing an event organised by the US Indian Community Foundation, Goyal said India had significantly expanded the scale of its trade negotiations in recent years, with another six to eight talks underway.Goyal said India's free trade agreements before 2014 covered economies representing about $10 trillion in GDP."In the last 4-4.5 years, we have decided to make free trade agreements with 31 developed and developing countries."The economies covered by the newer agreements represented about $60 trillion in GDP, he said."Some have been. Some will be in the next 6-8 months. In a way, you're talking about 70 trillion dollars," Goyal said.The minister said another six to eight negotiations were underway with economies representing about $15 trillion."So, India will become the centre of an international web of global trading relationships.Covering nearly 75-80 per cent of the world's economies," he said.Goyal said the widening trade network would give companies operating from India access to a larger international market and support deeper integration into international supply chains. India has been pursuing trade negotiations to seek greater access for its goods and services and deeper integration into global value chains. Such agreements typically seek to lower or eliminate tariffs on specified goods while establishing rules covering services, investment and other areas of economic activity.Goyal urged American and Indian-American entrepreneurs to participate in India's economic expansion as the country works towards growing from a $4 trillion economy today to a $30 trillion economy by 2047."The opportunity that a $4 trillion economy today, which is working towards becoming a $30 trillion economy by 2047, provides to you for your businesses, for your children and for the shared prosperity of the United States of America and India," Goyal said."This big opportunity, you don't have to leave it. I invite you to join it," he said.Goyal said India was moving towards its goal of becoming Viksit Bharat by 2047, when it marks 100 years of independence. He said India's 1.4 billion people had made a collective decision to build a developed country and achieve a better quality of life."India is moving ahead fast and fast," Goyal said, describing India as the fastest-growing economy and highlighting opportunities for investors and technology companies."India has the strength of a young country. India has the enthusiasm... We are a young nation of aspirational boys and girls," he said, adding "Our average age is 30 years!"Goyal also pointed to changes in manufacturing, infrastructure, digital connectivity and defence production, citing the expansion of commercial airports, growth in defence exports, the spread of 5G connectivity and the development of the startup ecosystem.During his Chicago visit, Goyal met US businesses, startups and professional groups to discuss investment, expansion and greater India-US collaboration.He met Juan Ricardo Luciano, Chair of the Board and CEO of Archer Daniels Midland (ADM), and discussed opportunities for the company to expand its presence and investments in India.“With our rapidly expanding food processing sector, modernizing agricultural value chains, and massive consumer base, India offers tremendous potential for sustainable growth and long term collaboration,” he said.Goyal also held talks with Aon CEO Greg Case on the company's operations in India and scope for further expansion. He highlighted “India's growing strengths as a global hub for talent, innovation and business services, and the potential for deeper India-US business partnerships.”On artificial intelligence, Goyal met Paul Grewal, Chief Legal and Global Affairs Officer at Cognition, and exchanged views on leveraging the company's artificial intelligence solutions and deepening its presence in India.His discussions with the US-India Business Council (USIBC) focused on startups and innovation. Goyal delivered the keynote address at a USIBC roundtable in Chicago on ‘Startups & Innovation: Scaling Ideas, Investment and Growth’.The roundtable covered venture investment, commercialisation and corporate partnerships to help Indian and US startups scale across markets. Goyal also explored opportunities to deepen India-US innovation linkages and support the next generation of high-growth enterprises.Goyal said that government institutions, including Invest India, could assist businesses through their investment journey and help promote trade, investment, tourism and technology transfers."The United States of America has capital strength, technology strength. India has ambition," he said.His engagements also included an interaction with the leadership and members of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) from its Chicago, Michigan and Ohio chapters.“Chartered Accountants have a pivotal role in strengthening this partnership by helping businesses navigate cross-border taxation, regulatory compliance and financial governance, while making Indian enterprises investment-ready for global capital,” Goyal said in his post on X.Goyal was in Chicago after representing India at the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee. During the visit, he also met American companies and investors and held several one-on-one meetings with large investors.The minister shared details of his Chicago engagements on his official X account, highlighting opportunities for investment, innovation and stronger business links between India and the US.
Article Summary: commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said India had significantly expanded the scale of its trade negotiations in recent years. Goyal urged American and Indian-American entrepreneurs to participate in India's economic expansion as the country works towards growing from a $4 trillion economy today to a $30 trillion economy by 2047.

Article Title: 'I am not an astrologer': Principal secy to PM declines to predict India's next GDP quarter
Article Text:
File photo: Principal secretary to PM PK Mishra

What is the next GDP number expected to show?

Why are growth forecasts being revised upwards?

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister’s principal secretary PK Mishra on Friday declined to predict India’s GDP performance for the next quarter, saying, “I am not an astrologer to predict. You will see when it is announced.”Mishra’s comment came as India’s economy enters the second quarter of FY27 after recording stronger-than-expected growth of 7.8% in the April-June period. The latest finance ministry assessment has put growth in the July-September quarter at an estimated 7.3%, suggesting that the economy may have maintained its momentum even as the pace moderated from the previous quarter.The finance ministry’s latest Monthly Economic Review, released on Thursday, projected real GDP growth at 7.3% for the September quarter through its nowcasting model. That would be lower than the 7.8% recorded in Q1, but would still point to continued expansion at a relatively strong pace.The ministry said growth momentum had continued into the second quarter, although at a more measured pace. E-way bill generation and manufacturing PMI showed some moderation, while services activity strengthened in August, supported by new business and employment.Electricity and fuel consumption also remained healthy, bank credit continued to expand and production of capital and infrastructure goods pointed to continued strength in investment.Automobile sales showed healthy growth across rural and urban markets, indicating broad-based consumption, the ministry said.The latest estimate follows a stronger-than-expected first quarter. India’s GDP grew 7.8% in April-June, beating the RBI’s earlier projection of 7% and marking the highest first-quarter growth in the current GDP series.The stronger Q1 performance has prompted several global institutions to raise their forecasts for India’s growth for FY27.The OECD has raised its forecast to 7.1% from 6.3%, while S&P Global Ratings and the Asian Development Bank now expect 7% growth. Fitch has raised its projection to 6.9%, while Moody’s has also revised its forecast to 7%. The RBI’s FY27 growth estimate stands at 6.7%.The upgrades have been linked to resilient domestic demand, investment, manufacturing activity and government spending. The ADB has also pointed to continued strength in services, manufacturing and consumption.Earlier GDP reports showed that the Q1 expansion was supported by broad-based growth, with real GVA rising 8.2%. Gross fixed capital formation grew 11.9%, while private final consumption expenditure rose 7.1%. Manufacturing grew 9.0%, while financial, real estate and professional services expanded 12.1%.But the stronger growth outlook comes against a backdrop of continuing global uncertainty.The finance ministry has flagged the impact of the West Asia conflict on energy markets and trade routes, while warning that geopolitical tensions and supply-chain disruptions could keep energy prices volatile and tighten global financial conditions.The RBI has similarly said the Indian economy has remained resilient, but identified geopolitical tensions and weather-related uncertainties as key downside risks. It also noted that the sharp rise in oil prices following the escalation of the West Asia conflict could revive inflationary pressures and disrupt supply chains.The OECD has also warned that reduced purchasing power could weaken growth in the second half of the year, while the agencies have flagged higher energy prices, inflation and geopolitical uncertainty as risks to the outlook.
Article Summary: PM's principal secretary PK Mishra declined to predict India's GDP performance for the next quarter. India’s economy enters the second quarter of FY27 after recording stronger-than-expected growth of 7.8% in the April-June period. The latest finance ministry assessment has put growth in the July-September quarter at an estimated 7.3%.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: 'Oil's' well in September: How India kept crude flowing amid the energy crisis
Article Text:
India's crude imports hit year-high in September

Country Imports Russia 1,872 Iraq 525 Saudi Arabia 517 UAE 438 Kuwait 335 Venezuela 196 Nigeria 137 Oman 132 US 125 Qatar 105

(Figures in thousand barrels per day; info credit: ET)

How India kept its crude flowing

Why Middle Eastern crude matters to Indian refiners

More operations resume

India has kept the crude flowing even as the Middle East conflict has choked global energy supply chains for over seven months. Imports surged to a year-high of 5.26 million barrels a day (mbd) in September, powered by a surprise jump in Gulf supplies.The rise in shipments from the region helped bring more Middle Eastern crude back into India’s import basket, with Iraq emerging as the country’s second-largest supplier behind Russia for the first time since the US-Iran conflict began in February.The surge was broad-based across the Gulf, with Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar together accounting for 39% of India’s total crude imports in September, according to Kpler. This comes after supplies from some of these countries had dropped sharply following the start of the Iran war on February 28, making the renewed flow of Gulf crude a notable shift in India’s import basket.Iraq supplied 525,000 barrels per day to India in September, putting it behind only Russia. Saudi Arabia followed closely with 517,000 bpd, while the UAE supplied 438,000 bpd. Kuwait also saw a notable jump, sending 335,000 bpd to India, its highest volume in a year, according to ET.The return of Iraqi and Kuwaiti crude marks a significant shift in India’s import flows. Supplies from both countries had nearly disappeared from India’s import slate for months following the start of the Middle East conflict on February 28. Their return, alongside higher shipments from other Gulf producers, helped push India’s overall crude imports to their highest level in a year.The increase in Gulf shipments has been supported by a workaround being used by Gulf producers and traders to move crude through the Strait of Hormuz.Dozens of large crude carriers are crossing the waterway with their Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders switched off. The cargo is then transferred through ship-to-ship (STS) operations in UAE and Omani waters.Other vessels subsequently carry the crude to customers, while the original carriers return to Gulf terminals for another run. National oil companies in the Gulf, along with some global traders, are arranging ships and taking the risk of crossing the Strait of Hormuz even as some attacks on vessels continue to be reported.The sharp increase in crude moving through the strait has also raised questions about whether Iran’s control over the waterway is weakening.The restoration of Gulf supplies has provided relief to Indian refiners, many of which are configured to process Middle Eastern crude."Increased Middle East barrels availability not only helps restore some of the lost supply but also provides access to crude grades with relatively strong middle-distillate yields, which align well with India's domestic product demand slate," said Nikhil Dubey, lead analyst, refining at commodity analytics firm Kpler.The increase in Middle Eastern crude availability comes after the recent passage of the Graham Bill, which empowers the US president to impose tariffs of up to 100% on India and other buyers of Russian oil.For Indian refiners, the additional Gulf supplies therefore provide another source of crude if their exposure to Russian barrels needs to be reduced."Ample Middle East barrels availability provides Indian refiners with additional sourcing optionality should they need to reduce their exposure to Russian barrels," Dubey was cited by ET as saying.The flow of crude has also been supported by the resumption of Saudi Arabia’s crucial East-West pipeline. The pipeline, which was attacked by the Houthis in September, has resumed operations and begun loading crude at the Red Sea port of Yanbu.With Gulf producers and traders continuing to organise shipments, crude from the Middle East has made up a larger share of India’s September import basket. The combination of increased Gulf availability, vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz and ship-to-ship transfers in UAE and Omani waters has kept crude moving to Indian refiners amid the energy supply disruption.The flow of energy through the Strait of Hormuz has also picked up, despite the continuing Middle East crisis and security concerns. LNG cargoes exiting the waterway rose to 19 in September from 15 in June, according to S&P Global Energy, while Kpler counted 21 cargoes.More QatarEnergy-linked vessels have also reappeared west of the strait, with one now offloading its cargo at India’s Hazira port. However, the sustainability of these flows through winter remains uncertain, with vessels continuing to make “dark transits” by switching off their AIS transponders.
Article Summary: India's crude imports hit year-high in September. Surge was broad-based across the Gulf, with Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar together accounting for 39% of India’s total crude imports. Iraq emerged as the country's second-largest supplier behind Russia for the first time since the US-Iran conflict began.

Article Title: At over 3.3 lakh, EVs witness record registrations in September
Article Text: Chennai: September turned out to be a record month for electric vehicles, with total registrations across segments touching an all-time high of 3.3 lakh units. The final number is likely to be slightly higher as there is typically a time lag before all registrations are reflected on the Vahan dashboard.Last month was also the fourth consecutive month in which EV registrations crossed the 3-lakh mark, signalling sustained momentum for battery-powered vehicles in the country.The sales surge in Sept was broad-based, with both electric two-wheelers (E2Ws) and passenger vehicles posting new monthly records. E2Ws led the charge, with registrations climbing to a record 2.07 lakh units, registering significant year-on-year growth.TVS Motor more than doubled its volumes year-on-year to about 54,000 units, as its monthly volumes bounced back to above the 50,000 mark after falling below that level in Aug. Bajaj also more than doubled its volumes year-on-year to about 48,400 units, while Ather's volumes stood at about 30,500 units, compared with 19,620 units in Sept 2025. Hero, Ola and Greaves sold more than 24,300 units, 13,450 units and 9,300 units, respectively.Electric passenger vehicles (e-PVs), too, hit a new high of around 36,000 units, almost double the volume sold in Sept 2025, indicating that electric cars are steadily gaining traction despite their relatively higher upfront costs.Tata remained the leader with e-PV sales of about 14,712 units (7340 units in Sep'25). Mahindra occupied the No. 2 spot with sales of 7,742 units (3783 units) and widened its gap with the third-ranked JSW MG Motor, which sold 5,226 units in Sept this year (4800 units). VinFast sold 2,960 units (just 6 units in Sept 25). Electric three-wheeler sales also bounced back in Sept to more than 86,000 units, compared with around 80,000 units in Aug and 88,315 units in July. In Sept 2025, sales stood at 61,434 units.
Article Summary: The sales surge in Sept was broad-based, with both electric two-wheelers (E2Ws) and passenger vehicles posting new monthly records. TVS Motor more than doubled its volumes year-on-year to about 54,000 units, as its monthly volumes bounced back to above the 50,000 mark.

Article Title: Irdai plan to help check mis-selling, raise returns
Article Text:
Irdai plan to help check mis-selling

What are the measures taken by the regulator on insurance distribution ?

Why have the shares of insurers, insurance distribution companies and banks fallen following the proposals?

What's new for customers

Which category of distributor is likely to be the most affected?

What about impact on individual agents?

What about general insurance?

What is the connection between high commissions and mis-selling?

MUMBAI: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai) introduced statutory caps on commissions and expenses of management (EoM) to put an end to commission-driven bidding wars and excessive upfront distributor payouts, ensuring cost efficiencies are directly passed on to policyholders through lower premiums, improved investment returns, and reduced mis-selling.Irdai has proposed moving insurance distribution away from a predominantly acquisition-and-commission model towards one focused on cost control, persistency, transparency and customer protection. The proposals include product-level commission caps, effort-based remuneration, restrictions on bundling insurance with loans and changes to the timing of life insurance commissions. The measures, however, are still proposals, not final regulations, with the consultation process open until Oct 25, 2026.Irdai has proposed bringing back product-level commission caps that were removed in 2023. For example, first-year commissions for life insurance distribution entities could be capped at 20% for policies with premium-paying terms of 10 years or more, while health insurance commissions could be capped at 15% in the first year and 5% on renewals. The proposals have raised concerns about the revenue of brokers, online aggregators, corporate agents and banks that earn significant income from insurance distribution.Insurance brokers, digital distribution platforms and other intermediaries that depend heavily on commission income appear more exposed, followed by banks and NBFCs with significant bancassurance or credit-linked insurance income. PB Fintech, the parent of Policybazaar, fell 36% on Sept 24, while Turtlemint fell 20%; shares of several banks also declined. Analysts said revenues of brokers, banks and non-bank lenders would be hit more than those of individual agents.Irdai has also proposed effort-based commissions, under which remuneration would be linked to factors such as product complexity, the effort involved in selling and servicing the policy, and the distribution channel. This could reduce payouts on products where commissions are rather high relative to the effort involved.Individual agents are also subject to product-wise commission caps, but the impact is expected to be lower than for brokers, banks and other large distribution channels. The proposals provide relatively higher commission ceilings for agents in some products and additional incentives for business from rural and underserved areas.The impact on non-life insurance is less clear. In motor insurance, third-party premiums are regulated, and Irdai has proposed eliminating commission on third-party motor insurance. In health insurance, a reduction in sales incentives could affect new policy additions; if healthier customers are less inclined to buy while people with higher health risks continue to seek cover, insurers could face adverse selection. Property insurance pricing is also influenced by the global reinsurance cycle.High commissions can create an incentive to sell products that generate greater remuneration for distributors rather than products that best suit customers. The concern is particularly relevant to bancassurance, where banks distribute insurance alongside their other financial products. Irdai’s proposals seek to address this by capping commissions, changing structure of life insurance payouts and restricting bundling of insurance with loans.
Article Summary: Irdai has proposed moving insurance distribution away from a predominantly acquisition-and-commission model. The proposals include product-level commission caps, effort-based remuneration, restrictions on bundling insurance with loans. Analysts said revenues of brokers, banks and non-bank lenders would be hit more than those of individual agents.

Article Title: Sea of red for most asset classes
Article Text:
Dalal Street ends week in red

MUMBAI: Nine months into 2026, most asset classes in the domestic market are signalling red in their respective year-to-date return columns.Data shows that so far this year, while sensex has given a negative return of 16%, Nifty has returned 15% in the red. In the bond segment also, with yields rising, investors have seen negative returns in their portfolio.Internationally, gold and silver prices have given negative returns. Although the rupee has weakened 7% so far in the year, domestic returns are in low single digits in gold and negative in silver.Only investors in crude oil have made good money—thanks mainly to the US-Iran war in the Persian Gulf that has led to a 67% gain in Brent crude. Outside of the popular assets, copper has given a smart return. The red metal has jumped from the $5.6/ounce level at the start of the year to the $6.5 level now, a 15% return. Looking ahead, inflationary expectations due to rising crude oil prices and, along with them, a weak rupee, could spook investors.A recent report by SBI Mutual Fund warned that inflation was a unifying macro theme of the year. For one, a delayed monsoon and lingering weather effects have depressed sowing activity and lifted food price risks, posing near-term challenges for rural incomes, the report said.The fund house also pointed out that input costs—from power and fuel in cement, to needle coke in electrodes, to milk procurement, freight, labour and packaging—are broadening rather than easing.“These pressures are already driving selective price hikes across FMCG, food diagnostics, consumer staples and several industrial categories. The ability to pass on these costs varies widely by sector. Fertilisers, agrochemicals and speciality chemicals face the most severe cost mismatches, with fertiliser economics particularly dependent on additional subsidy support as subsidy rates have not kept pace with raw material inflation. The world is in an inflationary boom, not yet an inflationary bust. A further rise in oil, or high bond yields starting to hurt growth, could tip it into a bust,” the report said.On the equities front, the fund house’s asset allocation framework continues to favour a 60:40 equity–fixed income allocation (versus a 50:50 benchmark). “It projects an early-teens equity CAGR at the large-cap index level over three years. Historically, a low level of market polarisation supports a tilt towards large caps.” On the debt side, the report said that the shorter end of the yield curve is offering relatively attractive opportunities, meaning investments in short-term papers are better bets than medium- or long-term ones.In the short run, RBI policy decision will be the key domestic trigger, with pressure to support the rupee and contain imported inflation strengthening expectations of a rate hike, said Vinod Nair, head of research, Geojit Investments. “With corporate earnings for Q2 expected to be softer than Q1, sentiment is likely to remain fragile. A meaningful de-escalation in West Asia could trigger a sharp relief rally. Until then, investors should stay selective, favouring earnings visibility. ”
Article Summary: Most asset classes in the domestic market are signalling red in their respective year-to-date return columns. While sensex has given a negative return of 16%, Nifty has returned 15% in the red. In the bond segment also, with yields rising, investors have seen negative returns in their portfolio.

Article Title: Cheaper Scotch nudges buyers up the whisky shelf
Article Text:
CRIEFF, SCOTLAND - NOVEMBER 05: Members of the public hold up whisky glasses at Glenturret Distillery in an attempt to set a record for the most people to raise a dram toast at the same time on November 5, 2015 in Crieff, Scotland. The event is being staged to celebrate 240 years of making whisky at Glenturret which is one of Scotlands oldest distilleries. (Photo by Jeff J Mitchell/Getty Images)

BENGALURU

: For India’s whisky drinkers, the next label up is moving a little closer. Cheaper Scotch is narrowing the price gaps between familiar bottles, giving some shoppers a reason to reconsider their usual purchase and Indian whisky makers fresh competition on the shelf.At Tonique in Bengaluru, operations head Nandish says some customers who usually buy Black & White are choosing Johnnie Walker Red Label or Black Label. All three are blended Scotches owned by Diageo.Diageo confirmed that Karnataka prices for 750ml bottles fell from Rs 2,810 to Rs 2,620 for Red Label and from Rs 4,005 to Rs 3,645 for Black Label since September. Nandish puts Black & White at Rs 2,365, leaving a Rs 255 step up to Red Label.The India-UK trade agreement halves whisky import tariffs from 150% to 75%. Retail prices also reflect state taxes and where spirits are bottled. Diageo, the first to start discounting prices, said that price revisions had reached seven states and were underway in four other markets. Delhi and Haryana had yet to see changes.Nandish said J&B had dropped from Rs 2,835 to Rs 1,375 per 750ml bottle, attributing the reduction to local bottling.Diageo has not confirmed that explanation. Tonique’s Blenders Pride Premium Collection shelf price was Rs 1,430 for the same volume.The overlap extends to Indian whiskies: 750ml Woodburns was tagged Rs 2,500, while Paul John Nirvana, an Indian single malt, was Rs 2,360.Competition is also sharpening among single malts. At Tonique, Glenfiddich 12 was priced at Rs 5,275 for 700ml, down from Rs 5,610.“Scotch has decades of familiarity, strong equity and cultural associations,” said John Distilleries, which makes Paul John. Nirvana’s appeal rested on Indian provenance, craftsmanship and flavour, it said.“Greater accessibility of established Scotch single malts certainly increases competitive intensity,” the company added. It would assess price dynamics while continuing to introduce more consumers to Indian single malt.Amrut Amalgam was tagged Rs 2,000 for 500ml at Tonique. Amrut Fusion’s Karnataka MRP of Rs 3,500 for 750ml sits just Rs 145 below Black Label, a blended Scotch. Amrut says the growing price overlap has not significantly disturbed its business.“At this point, we are not seeing any indication of Amrut aficionados switching to Scotch purely based on pricing,” said Thrivikram G. Nikam, Amrut Distilleries’ joint managing director. He said there were no specific repricing plans.Radico Khaitan similarly said it was focusing on premium positioning for Royal Ranthambore and Rampur.“Rather than responding and adjusting to short-term price movements, we remain focused on strengthening the premium positioning and value proposition of our brands,” its spokesperson said.Radico said Karnataka’s tax overhaul, effective in May, had already lowered Rampur Indian Single Malt’s price from Rs 7,240 to Rs 6,380 per 750ml bottle. It reported continued double-digit growth in the state.
Article Summary: Cheaper Scotch is narrowing the price gaps between familiar bottles. India-UK trade agreement halves whisky import tariffs from 150% to 75%. Retail prices also reflect state taxes and where spirits are bottled. Diageo, the first to start discounting prices, said that price revisions had reached seven states.

Article Title: Father got 3 bigha of land from Himachal government, but patta was never signed; why HC allowed married daughter's inheritance appeal & what role Hindu Succession Act plays
Article Text:
The Hindu Succession Act, 1956, does not distinguish between married and unmarried Hindu daughters when determining inheritance rights. (Image for representative purpose only)

Why did the daughter win the case?

You are allotted land by the state government under Nautor rules, but what happens after your death? Can your married daughter inherit it? In one such case, the court has ruled in favour of the daughter, citing the Hindu Succession Act.Let’s read on to know what the case is about:In 1972, the Himachal Pradesh government allotted three bigha and two biswas of agricultural land in Shimla to a person under the Nautor rules for cultivation. Although a revenue assistant handed over possession of the plot, the officials concerned never signed the patta, or the formal land revenue document, for reasons that remain unknown.Following the man’s death in 1990, his wife approached the authorities seeking the patta. However, the document remained unsigned even though it was ready. Consequently, neither the man or his wife’s name was entered in the land's revenue records through mutation, as the necessary paperwork had not been executed, according to an ET report.His wife died in 2012, leaving behind their only daughter, who subsequently approached the revenue authorities once again for issuance of the patta.This time, however, her request was reportedly rejected outright on the ground that married daughters were ineligible for land under the Nautor rules.The daughter maintained that she was not seeking a fresh allotment but merely requesting the patta for land already granted to her deceased father, claiming entitlement as a Class I legal heir under the Hindu Succession Act.Her counsel moved the court and relied on the Himachal Pradesh Nautor Land Rules, 1968. He submitted that the rules provide that a son or daughter cannot apply for Nautor land while the father is alive, and a wife cannot apply when her husband is alive.The exception is where the son, daughter or wife establishes that the father or husband, as applicable, has disinherited or separated them, or has renounced the world.The counsel argued that the rules contain no provision barring married daughters from seeking a patta.He further submitted that, even otherwise, the established legal position is that a married daughter who remains dependent on her parents cannot be denied any entitlement she may have as a Class-I legal heir of the original allottee.After examining Rules 7 and 8 of the Himachal Pradesh Nautor Land Rules, the High Court observed that Rule 7 does not indicate anywhere that a married daughter is disqualified from applying for Nautor land.Under Rule 8, a son or daughter cannot seek Nautor land while their father is alive, just as a wife cannot apply when her husband is living. The restriction, however, does not apply if the son, daughter or wife establishes that the father or husband, as applicable, has disinherited or separated them, or has renounced the world. In such circumstances, they become eligible to apply for Nautor land.The court observed that the provisions permit sons and daughters to seek Nautor land, with the restriction applying specifically during the father's lifetime.The Himachal Pradesh High Court said: “There is no specific rule under Nautor rules that debar a married daughter from claiming land under the said Rules.”In 1980, the Himachal Pradesh government issued a clarification circular proposing a review of sanctions and their re-issuance in favour of Category-I legal heirs under the Hindu Succession Act.It stated that where married daughters were among the Class-I heirs, the land should not be sanctioned in their names. Instead, the remaining legal heirs were to be considered for allotment.The High Court held that the communication was merely an administrative clarification and could not supersede statutory rules that carry the force of law.The court also noted that under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, married daughters are now recognised as having coparcenary rights. It clarified that the daughter in this case was not seeking a patta on the ground that she was the unmarried daughter of her parents. Her claim was based on her status as a Class-I legal heir, through which she sought issuance of the patta in her favour.The court observed that her application under the Nautor provisions did not contain any request for a fresh allotment of land under those Rules. Instead, she had specifically sought permission and grant of 03-02 bighas of land in Shimla district, referring to the sanction order and compensation deposited by her mother.The High Court accordingly allowed the daughter's appeal and directed the authorities to reconsider her case in light of the court's findings. It asked them to complete the exercise, preferably within two months from the date of the order.Amitraj Kaushal, Advocate at Supreme Court of India, told ET that the daughter won because the Himachal Pradesh High Court found no explicit provision in the Himachal Pradesh Nautor Land Rules, 1968, that prevents a married daughter from inheriting Nautor land as a legal heir.Kaushal says the court additionally considered the evolution of the law towards recognising equal inheritance and coparcenary rights for daughters. It also drew upon the Supreme Court's reasoning that denying married daughters such rights solely because of their marital status is rooted in a gender stereotype. The rejection order was accordingly set aside.Kaushal explains that the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, does not distinguish between married and unmarried Hindu daughters when determining inheritance rights. Marriage, by itself, cannot disqualify a daughter from inheriting her parents' property.Kaushal says: "Where a Hindu dies intestate, succession is governed by the statutory scheme, and daughters who fall within the applicable Class-I category inherit along with other Class-I heirs, subject to the specific facts and nature of the property."In other words, when a Hindu daughter qualifies as a surviving Class-I heir, her marital status alone cannot be used to deny her inheritance.
Article Summary: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956, does not distinguish between married and unmarried Hindu daughters when determining inheritance rights. The Himachal Pradesh High Court ruled in favour of the daughter. The court observed that the provisions permit sons and daughters to seek Nautor land, with the restriction applying specifically during the father's lifetime.

Article Title: India-US trade deal not imminent, PM Modi-Trump may hold another call soon: US trade representative
Article Text:
Piyush Goyal with Jamieson Greer

Goyal, Greer hold talks in Milwaukee

What's after February framework?

The India-US trade agreement is in the "short strokes" of negotiations, but the deal is not yet imminent. United States Trade Representative (USTR) Jamieson Greer has indicated that discussions between the two sides are continuing over unresolved issues. He added that PM Modi and US President Donald Trump could speak again soon to review the progress of the negotiations.The US trade chief added that the two sides have identified the full set of items that were still proving to be sticking points and were working towards resolving them.Commenting on the negotiations, the Greer said, "We had a very constructive conversation with Minister Piyush Goyal... We are continually trying to finish the trade deal with India, we are in the short strokes. I think we are towards the end of it. President Trump and the Prime Minister Modi had a constructive call yesterday morning. At the same time, I don't think there is something imminent.”He added, “But we truly have identified the universe of items that are sticking points, and we are working diligently toward them. The President and the Prime Minister may have another call very soon on this just to assess progress and where we are."The latest comments came after Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal held talks with Greer on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee. The meeting was part of ongoing bilateral efforts to conclude a "balanced and mutually beneficial" trade agreement between New Delhi and Washington.Goyal had earlier said that the discussions were aimed at an early conclusion of an interim agreement under the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA).In a post on X, he wrote, "Met USTR Jamieson Greer, US trade representative, on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee. Had a productive discussion with USTR Greer towards early conclusion of a mutually beneficial interim agreement under the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement. We also exchanged views on G20 deliberations under US Chairship."The talks between Goyal and Greer took place on Wednesday, the same day PM Modi and Trump held a telephone conversation. The two leaders discussed progress in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas of mutual interest.Ahead of Goyal's visit, the ministry said his discussions with the US counterpart would focus on advancing the Bilateral Trade Agreement and finalising an interim deal in line with the Joint Statement of February 7, 2026."Goyal will also engage bilaterally with his counterpart from the United States as part of ongoing efforts to advance a balanced and mutually beneficial India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) and finalise an interim deal in line with the Joint Statement of 7 February 2026."India and the US had announced in February this year that they had finalised the framework for the initial phase of the Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA). However, negotiations continued following changes in the US tariff landscape.Goyal had said on September 24 that the India-US trade pact was "done and dusted", but added that it would be executed once the US gives India the right competitive advantage over its competitors in the American market.Within the US market, India's primary regional competitors include China, Bangladesh and member states of ASEAN.
Article Summary: The India-US trade agreement is in the "short strokes" of negotiations, but the deal is not yet imminent. The two sides have identified the full set of items that were still proving to be sticking points and were working towards resolving them. PM Modi and US President Donald Trump could speak again soon to review the progress of the negotiations.

Article Title: Simi Singh: An Ireland dream, a life-threatening detour and the journey home
Article Text:
Simi Singh. (Photo by Donall Farmer/PA Images via Getty Images)

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of Simi Singh’s career do you find most inspiring? His journey from player to coach His resilience during health issues His achievements with the Irish national team His ability to adapt to life's challenges 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Simranjit Singh, known as Simi Singh in Ireland and across world cricket, had already retired in his mind when acute liver failure brought his career to a shuddering halt in 2024. But on Wednesday, he closed the chapter officially, announcing his retirement and bringing down the curtain on a remarkable 20-year association with Ireland, the country he moved to in 2006 to pursue hotel management, only to find a second life in cricket.Over his two decades in Ireland, the highs were incredibly high, but the lows were devastating as well.“I played international cricket, represented Ireland in the World Cup (T20), scored a century while batting at No. 8 against South Africa in ODIs and picked up a five-wicket haul as well. Recently, I came to know that I have the best economy rate in ODIs (3.99), with Rashid Khan second. When I packed my bags and left for Ireland as a teenager, playing cricket was not something I had in my mind. It was special,” Simi told TimesofIndia.com.“The people at Cricket Ireland were not surprised because, even before this, I was not being considered for selection. It had become difficult to play professional cricket, especially with my recovery still going on. So I thought it was better to properly close things and make an official announcement so that everyone knew,” added Simi, who played 35 ODIs and 53 T20Is for Ireland.In early 2024, Simi’s life was turned upside down after he developed a mysterious fever. Doctors in Ireland were unable to find the underlying cause and his health began to deteriorate. He eventually moved to India in search of better medical opinions, only to discover that he had developed acute liver failure. His wife, Agamdeep Kaur, donated part of her liver to save his life.“My wife is my guardian angel. She was God-sent. She gave me a new life. It was a torrid time for the family,” he said.“Now I have moved back to Mohali. Recovery is still going on. There is improvement, but it is slow. I will survive,” he added.It was never all hunky-dory for Simi in Ireland. With tough residency rules, his ECB Level 2 coaching qualification and certification as a personal trainer helped him stay afloat before he eventually broke into the national team. Now, the coaching qualification he earned all those years ago has come to the fore. He has opened his own cricket academy in Mohali, the city where he toiled during his formative years and represented Punjab successfully at the U-14 and U-17 levels.“For now, I am not running the academy myself. I have completed Level 2 with the England Cricket Board, and I am thinking of doing Level 3. Then we will see what opportunities come up,” he said.When Simi left India in 2006, he was frustrated that his cricketing career had failed to take off. Nearly two decades later, the 39-year-old looks back at his journey with a sense of gratitude — or shukrana, as he puts it in Punjabi.“I am relaxed here. My parents are fine. My dad even came to the ground with me. It is good to be back home. My parents were getting old. I am not missing any festivals. Now the coming and going and all that headache is over,” he said.For someone who left India as a teenager without cricket even figuring in his plans, Simi’s journey has come full circle. Ireland gave him a career he had stopped believing was possible. Then he fought a life-threatening illness but his wife gave him a second chance at life. Now, with cricket behind him as a player, Simi wants to build the next chapter from Mohali, closer to home and with a renewed sense of gratitude.
Article Summary: Simi Singh, known as Simi Singh in Ireland and across world cricket, had already retired in his mind when acute liver failure brought his career to a shuddering halt in 2024. On Wednesday, he closed the chapter officially, announcing his retirement and bringing down the curtain on a remarkable 20-year association with Ireland. Simi played 35 ODIs and 53 T20Is for Ireland.

NEW DELHI: Across the open and women's sections at the Chess Olympiad, only one player won an individual gold medal for India at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. That was Chennai's 19-year-old Savitha Shri Baskar. Savitha was often the one India could rely on when the team was staring at heartbreak. With her games routinely going down to the wire, she was kept fuelled, game after game, by someone making sure she never had to think about anything other than the board during India's bronze-clinching campaign."If we wanted something, he was always there, giving us everything, like water, bananas, and for me, he was bringing endless coffees because I played till the last moment, making sure that I ate properly and got energy," Savitha recalled, before labelling Swayams Mishra as the "best captain ever".For Mishra, it was new territory in a role he'd long been adjacent to."I've been part of the women's team since 2022, but this was the first time I was captaining completely. In 2024, I had captained for a couple of games, but this was a completely new experience," he told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction."This time, I have to be there in the tournament hall with the players, especially in the critical games, so the emotions are completely different compared to when you are outside.That was slightly different, and not easy."The job, according to Mishra, was less about tactics and more about manoeuvres of a different kind."It was hectic and exhausting, because as a captain you try to follow all the games going on, not just one player's. At the same time, sometimes you see a player making a mistake; you want to do something, but you cannot; you just have to wait for it to unfold naturally," he admitted. What he could control, though, he controlled."What I tried to do is look at what the players needed. If there's a longer game, they needed some energy or something to eat, so I made sure they had it available instead of spending time getting it themselves around the third or fourth hour."Viewers watching the live broadcast of the games got to witness the results of that instinct in real time, with water bottles, bananas, and coffee cups appearing at just the right moments.The challenges for Swayams started even before the tournament. Getting the team to that stage was a project in itself, with busy, overlapping schedules making it difficult for the players to train together in person.With the help of the All India Chess Federation (AICF), the team turned to virtual camps in the run-up to the Olympiad."It all started with the camps, like organising the camp online, where we found that most of the players' schedules were very tight, so we held an online camp because players were not able to find a common timing to able to meet up with their busy schedules," Mishra revealed.The challenges followed the team in Samarkand, where India, like several other nations, faced accommodation and food issues."On the first day, with the issues with the stay, AICF stepped up, and the president Nitin Narang and the HOD Abhijit Kunte ensured that the players got the rooms first," he said. "President Narang was also present, and he went out of his way to help us in most of the things."Food then became another issue, with Mishra recalling that “when food was not very ideal, the options were not great, AICF made sure that food is Indian food people get so that they don't lack energy and they don't go like let's say their routine and other things are not disturbed as well.”The team bronze did not come easy, without its share of difficult calls. One of the toughest was deciding which four players from the five-member squad would take the board each round."For me, it was not easy choosing whom to play, because it was always a tricky call, with Savitha and Vantika performing very well on the last boards, and Vaishali also having good chances; we wanted her to play. It's a very hard call when one of your top players ends up not being in form, and the others are performing very well. Vaishali tried, gave her best, but it just wasn't meant to be," the captain, who then decided to keep the Women's World Championship challenger on the board for only six out of the eleven games, sighed.With Vaishali, who had just one win in the entire Olympiad and finished with a score of 2.5/6, due to challenge for the Women's World Championship title next year, Mishra also addressed whether this stretch of poor form carried any psychological weight into that bigger picture."We had a discussion, and she was not thinking at all about the World Championship. She wanted to just focus and give her best for India in this Olympiad, but it wasn't working out. I think she's strong enough, a professional player who should be able to get back much stronger and prove herself as a world champion as well. I wish she wins the World Championship.""Humpy on board one, I think, this would be her best Olympiad. India hadn't won a medal on board one for quite some time, and her winning one (a bronze with a score of 7/10), undefeated, against strong opposition, was very good. We were never on the back foot on board one," captain Mishra explained.Board two, however, told a different story."Vaishali started off decently. She had some tough opponents who didn't make mistakes and played precisely against her. Against Poland, that's where things changed — she had a better position, in fact, and wanted to win. There were a couple of chances to simplify into a draw, but she wanted to win, and in that process ended up making mistakes and losing," the coach added."Then she had another critical game against Kazakhstan, where she again had chances to equalise but wanted to win it for the team. A draw there would have given us 2-2, because Savitha's board wasn't clear yet. So she tried, and it backfired. You can say she was always there for the team, even if her performance wasn't great."By contrast, individual silver medalist Divya Deshmukh, scoring 6.5/10, emerged as one of the pillars."She took a lot of blacks, seven out of ten games, and was always ready whenever the team needed her. She had a consistent performance and gave us a couple of fast wins that put pressure on the other opponents."It came after a rough patch as Mishra continued, "She started completely out of form; Cairns Cup wasn't as per expectations, GCL wasn't great. But from there, she came back very strongly and was always reliable. She lost the last round, but she'd done her job by then."Vantika Agrawal, on board four for most of the tournament before Savitha's emergence, drew measured praise."She was consistent. There was one game, against China, that was very close, where she was close to a draw and missed something under pressure. Otherwise, she did her job, whatever was assigned to her, and gave us points on the last board," he added.And then Savitha. Mishra didn't hold back on addressing the scrutiny that had followed her selection."There were a lot of people who questioned her spot, journalists saying there are players higher than her, and so on. But according to the selection, she was qualified, and she'd won the Asian continental a couple of months ago. She'd also played the World Women's Team Championship, so I knew her as a team player always."Whenever we gave her the opportunity, she delivered. From round seven onwards, her form dropped slightly compared to the initial rounds as she was making some errors; the quality wasn't quite what she'd have expected. But she always compensated in the last hour, changing the result of the match completely. If India won a medal, we owe it to her."Asked whether anyone inside the camp was satisfied with bronze, Mishra didn't pretend otherwise."We are not satisfied. The colour of the medal would have been different, and we would have been much happier. But even in your not-so-good times, if you're able to get a medal, that shows how strong the team is. We expect to come back even stronger next year and win gold."I know people might be disappointed; the fans might be disappointed; we're equally disappointed. But everyone tried their best. The margins were very close."The tournament's bigger lesson, for him, had less to do with India specifically than with the state of women's chess as a whole."We did not underestimate anyone, but there were a lot of teams creating upsets. Mongolia, whom we played in round four, and Greece in round three, both ended up causing upsets elsewhere. Against the silver-winning Kazakh team, Mongolia were winning too, before it finished 2-2. In the last few Olympiads it was smooth sailing for the top seeds.This year, weaker teams were able to strike. That means chess is growing in general, especially women's chess. "ALSO READ: 'Unrealistic to win gold every single time': Captain Srinath Narayanan after India's silver at Chess Olympiad | Exclusive It's a tournament Mishra will remember as much for its margins as its medal, a campaign where India were, by his own description, "always on the wrong side of where we wanted to be", rescued more than once by a teenager fuelled on endless cups of coffee, and still, somehow, bronze rather than nothing at all.
Article Summary: India won bronze at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. Captain Swayams Mishra described the experience as hectic and exhausting. Savitha Shri Baskar was often the one India could rely on when the team was facing heartbreak.

Article Title: G7’s 100-million-barrel diesel fix: What happens after the emergency release
Article Text:
What happens after G7's emergency release

The replenishment challenge

How much is actually being added?

Supply routes under pressure

The G7 is tapping its emergency oil stash, with plans to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products to ease the diesel crunch. Earlier on Friday, the bloc said it would start opening the taps in the coming weeks, beginning with a “frontloaded substantial release” of diesel “immediately” and within the next 20 days. The remaining volumes will be released over four months.However, the strategy comes with its own share or risks and gaps.US President Donald Trump said that the diesel release would happen “immediately”, as fuel prices remain elevated across the US and Europe. The average US diesel price stood at $6.37 a gallon on Friday, according to AAA, after hitting a record $6.52 on September 22. In Europe too, diesel prices have reached record levels.France, which currently holds the rotating G7 presidency, announced the release after a videoconference led by President Emmanuel Macron, involving the G7 nations and EU representation. The move follows a March commitment by IEA members to release 426 million barrels, including around 92 million barrels from EU countries, largely refined products such as diesel, with Macron saying the latest release should add liquidity and lower prices.But the big question is whether the barrels coming out of emergency storage can keep pace with the pressures pushing prices higher.Russia has banned exports following Ukrainian drone strikes on its refineries, while refined fuel shipments from Persian Gulf producers have fallen because of war damage and blocked export routes.Though Europe does not import Russian diesel, countries such as Turkey and those in Latin America that buy it are now competing with Europe for the barrels still available.So, while the G7 is putting more fuel into the market, the squeeze on supplies has not necessarily disappeared. The emergency oil stash may offer some relief, but the supply problems behind the squeeze remain.The biggest risk identified by experts is what happens after the reserves have been used.Jim Krane, energy research fellow at Rice University's Baker Institute, told AP that the move could temporarily reduce retail fuel prices but would also leave Europe with less emergency cover.“Draining stocks will reduce retail fuel prices for a while, at the cost of leaving Europe with less emergency cover,” Krane said. “At some point in the future Europe and the rest of the G7 will have to refill their strategic reserves. Normally they try to do this when prices are low. Nobody knows when that will happen.
